s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual disturbance and endocrine dysfunction due to a large sellar/suprasellar mass
key_facts: 49-year-old woman
2-year history of chronic bitemporal headache
Unexplained easy fatigability
Progressive diminution of vision
Bitemporal homonymous hemianopia
Central hypothyroidism
Well-controlled hypertension
Large sellar/suprasellar mass on CT and MRI
Mass extends into both cavernous sinuses
Bony remodeling of the sella turcica and upper clivus
Heterogeneous low T1 signal on MRI
Intermediate high T2 signal on MRI
Small central areas of diffusion restriction on DWI
Mild patchy postcontrast enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Pituitary macroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large sellar/suprasellar mass with bony remodeling and endocrine dysfunction

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual disturbance and large sellar/suprasellar mass with calcification not mentioned but possible

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Dural-based mass with bony remodeling and possible endocrine dysfunction

shortlist.label: Pituitary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive features such as bony remodeling and possible cranial nerve involvement

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
shortlist.why_kept: Endocrine dysfunction and possible inflammatory origin of the sellar/suprasellar mass

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a large pituitary macroadenoma, including bitemporal headache, progressive diminution of vision, and a large sellar/suprasellar mass on CT and MRI. The presence of central hypothyroidism also supports this diagnosis, as pituitary macroadenomas can compress the pituitary gland and stalk, leading to hormonal deficiencies.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Typically presents in childhood or adolescence and often contains calcifications, which were not mentioned in the imaging findings

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Usually has a more homogeneous appearance on MRI and may have a dural tail sign, which was not described

rejected.label: Pituitary carcinoma
rejected.why: Rare and typically requires evidence of metastasis, which was not mentioned

rejected.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with symptoms of pituitary dysfunction and inflammation, and imaging findings often show a more diffuse and symmetric enlargement of the pituitary gland
